dct_description_sm: The purpose of this research is to examine if landscape scale carbon fluxes can capture the spatial heterogeneity that occurs across a palsa permafrost peatland.   Because of permafrost thaw various peatland microforms make a heterogeneous peatland complex resulting in a high spatial variability in net ecosystem exchanges.  Thawing permafrost results in large variations in surface elevations, water table depths, vegetation cover, and ground temperatures at scales of only a few meters.  Our research question is: can the spatially integrated ecosystem level net ecosystem exchange measured by the eddy covariance technique be explained by the light use efficient and respiration models of the component parts of the ecosystem based on the up-scaling using plant-functional types?
dct_title_s: Net ecosystem exchange (NEE) of a permafrost peat plateau
